findings.description: Components split between motion library (App.jsx sections) and CSS animations (PageTransition, modals, dropdowns, form inputs), risking inconsistent timing and harder maintenance.
Motion library adds ~237 kB gzip (vs. CSS-only ~7.87 kB). No code-splitting or lazy loading. For a cybersecurity dashboard, this is notable without corresponding performance gain.

useMotionPrefs is called in App.jsx main sections but not in child views. Users with reduced motion preference will see full spring animations in LaboratoriesView, LabComputersView, LiveAlertsView, CsvAnalyticsPage, and ComputerDetailView.

findings.issue: CSS animation tokens not utilized by motion library
findings.description: motion.js defines springs with hardcoded stiffness/damping but does not reference CSS custom properties (--ios-duration-*, --ios-ease). Global timing adjustments via CSS won't affect motion library animations.

findings.issue: Legacy CSS keyframes removed but PageTransition still uses CSS
findings.description: index.css comment states animations moved to motion library, yet PageTransition applies .ios-page-container class with iosPageEntrance CSS keyframe. Semantic confusion about which system handles animation.

findings.issue: Missing motion integration in child components
findings.description: LabComputersView, LiveAlertsView, CsvAnalyticsPage, ComputerDetailView do not import motion or useMotionPrefs. Tables and lists don't benefit from motion library exit animations or staggered reveals. ~60% of application remains static or CSS-based.

findings.issue: useMotionPrefs hook sets state on mount synchronously
findings.description: Hook uses useState and useEffect with synchronous setPrefersReducedMotion on media query change. Linter warns this can trigger cascading renders; React anti-pattern flagged by oxlint.

findings.issue: prefers-reduced-motion not respected by CSS animations
findings.description: No global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule in App.css. Modals, dropdowns, form inputs, nav items will animate at full speed even when user has reduced motion preference enabled in OS settings.
